text.p: Following are the highlights of main stories in Serbian and Montenegrin papers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- S E R B I A --
POLITIKA
- Serbian parliament to appoint a ten-member electoral supervising board on Monday. Five parliamentary parties which will take part in elections proposed their representatives.
- OSCE agreed to send its monitors to Serbia for the September 21 elections following Yugoslavia's request.

- Serbia's bank Vojvodjanska banka denied claims that foreign currency frozen on the accounts of Beogradska banka Cyprus affiliate were transferred to it. The assets were frozen following a suit filed by Slovenia which demanded the funds be included in the division of ex-Yugoslavia's assets.
- Serbia's firm Energoprojekt won a $6.5 million road reconstruction project in Bolivia.
- Domestic cigarette sales were up in July to 540 tonnes which is 86 percent more than June, say industry sources.
- Cargo storage of Belgrade airport is becoming too small for the 20 percent monthly increase of handled goods.
- Reconstruction works in metal complex Trepca worth some five million dollars will be completed next week.

- Serbian Renewal Movement (SPO) President Vuk Draskovic visited Kosovo, said resolution of the Kosovo issue should be sought within the scope of Serbia and on the basis of European and international standards.
- Montenegrin Constitutional Court says its decision to annul presidential candidacy of Momir Bulatovic is final and the Yugoslav Constitutional Court does not have the authority to revise it.
NASA BORBA

- The State Department extended support to Kosovo's autonomy but not to its independence during the visit of Democratic League of Kosovo President Ibrahim Rugova to Washington. President Bill Clinton said respect of human rights in Kosovo remains the key to lifting U.S. sanctions towards Yugoslavia.
- Adem Demaqi, president of the Parliamentary Party of Kosovo said autonomy is not an acceptable solution for Kosovo Albanians.

- The Serbian Student Movement will organise a baton race for Yugoslav President Slobodan Milosevic on his birthday, August 20 in a reinaction of the race run every year for late president Tito. This is within the scope of the "halt to tyranny" action.

- Serbian Renewal Movement (SPO) President Vuk Draskovic said on state television that election conditions were "better than ever in the past seven years" and there was no reason for his party to boycott the elections.
BORBA
- Representatives of Italian business association WIGWAM are interested in concrete agriculture and tourism projects in Yugoslavia.

- Yugoslavia does not have enough meat for exports and must take measures to protect its agriculture and livestock breeding, said vice president of the association of agricultural producers Jugoagrar Janos Platinus.
- Serbian Development Fund extended a seven million German mark credit to the mining-smelting complex Bor for the purchase of spare parts and raw materials for completing concluded export deals.
-- M O N T E N E G R O --
POBJEDA

- The Yugoslav Constitutional Court would flagrantly violate Yugoslavia's legal order if it considers president Momir Bulatovic's appeal on the ruling of the Montenegrin Constitutional Court, the Montenegrin court said in a press release.

- The 'recipe' of Serbian Radical Party leader Vojislav Seselj to introduce a state of emergency in Montenegro would result in a rapid disintegration of the federation, said Montenegrin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic.
- Marble production company from Danilovgrad Mermer holding has been privatised. All 340 employees will retain their jobs. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 311 4305
